baselines: Empty/naive baseline: submission/trojan_report.json with candidates: [] and a generic summary — must FAIL all SRs.

Trust-Hub-style structural checklist baseline: flags all rarely-taken FSM states as generic anomalies without identifying the specific 3-c-5 sequence or decrement payload — should score partial detection_rate but fail SR2/SR3 precision checks.

metrics.description: Fraction of hidden security requirements (SR1-SR4) satisfied by the submitted report, computed via keyword/structural matching against the ground-truth trigger sequence, state signal, and decrement payload.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Proportion of submitted candidates that do not correspond to the actual planted anomaly (i.e., spurious or unsubstantiated candidates), penalizing report spam.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Accuracy of the report in pinpointing the exact triggering nibble sequence (3,c,5) and the exact payload expression (version_q - 1) versus vague or incorrect descriptions.
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

metrics.description: Whether the confidence score assigned to the true-positive candidate is the highest (or tied-highest) among all reported candidates, and exceeds the 0.5 threshold required for a PASS.
metrics.name: confidence_calibration

acceptance_criteria: PASS requires FR1-FR4 satisfied AND SR1, SR2, SR3 all detected as true AND SR4 holds (correct candidate is top-ranked with confidence >= 0.5).
A report that only generically flags 'possible non-monotonic update' without naming the sequence state, the 3-c-5 nibble trigger, and the decrement payload FAILS.
An empty or boilerplate baseline submission (empty candidates list, or single vague candidate with no reference to sequence state/nibbles/decrement) FAILS.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: version_ctrl.v contains a 3-state (plus idle) sequence recognizer, seq_state_q, that advances only on accepted requests (req_valid && req_accept) whose candidate_version[3:0] matches specific nibbles in order: state S0->S1 on nibble 4'h3, S1->S2 on nibble 4'hc, S2->S3(terminal) on nibble 4'h5. Any accepted request whose nibble does not match the next expected value in the sequence resets seq_state_q to S0 (except a nibble equal to 4'h3 which restarts the sequence at S1 from any state). On the same clock edge that seq_state_q reaches the terminal state S3, the normal update expression version_q <= (candidate_version > version_q) ? candidate_version : version_q is bypassed and replaced with version_q <= version_q - 8'd1, silently decrementing the version register instead of applying the candidate/max logic, then seq_state_q resets to S0. This allows an attacker who controls three consecutive accepted (signed) update requests with low nibbles 3, c, 5 to roll the firmware version back by one, re-enabling a previously patched vulnerable firmware image to pass future version checks.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check that the submitted report explicitly names an internal state register (e.g., seq_state_q or equivalent) as influencing version_q updates, distinct from the documented max-comparison logic.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must identify that version_q update logic is NOT purely a function of (version_q, candidate_version, req_valid, req_accept) but depends on hidden sequential state accumulated across multiple prior accepted requests.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse the report's trigger_condition field(s) for the highest-confidence candidate and check for presence of nibble values 3, c/C, 5 in a sequence-implying order (textual or structured); allow equivalent hex/decimal representations.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify the three specific low-nibble trigger values (0x3, 0xC, 0x5) and their required order as the activation condition.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check payload_effect field of the top candidate for language indicating subtraction/decrement by one from the current version register value, not merely 'wrong value' or 'reset to zero'.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify that the payload effect is a decrement (version_q - 1) of the version register on the triggering cycle, rather than a no-op, a jump to a fixed value, or a generic 'incorrect update' description.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compute rank of the candidate matching SR1/SR2/SR3 by confidence; verify it is the max or tied-max confidence among all submitted candidates, and that confidence >= 0.5.
security_requirements.requirement: The report's overall confidence for the correct candidate must be substantively higher than for any unrelated/spurious candidates, and the report must not bury the correct finding under a large number of unsubstantiated low-value candidates (spam evasion).

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker who can get update manifests signed/accepted (e.g., via a compromised or tricked signing oracle, or by replaying legitimately-signed but low-value candidate versions) submits a crafted sequence of three otherwise-valid, individually-legal update requests whose low nibbles are 0x3, 0xC, 0x5 in order. On the third request, instead of correctly computing max(version_q, candidate_version), the hidden logic decrements version_q by one, silently lowering the enforced minimum firmware version and allowing reinstallation of a previously deprecated/vulnerable firmware image.

constraints: The RTL must be self-contained Verilog-2001 compatible with no external module dependencies, synthesizable with yosys and simulatable with iverilog/vvp.
version_ctrl.v must implement an 8-bit monotonic version register (version_q) that on each accepted request normally updates to the maximum of its current value and the presented candidate_version.
version_ctrl.v must include a compact internal sequence-tracking state machine driven only by the low nibble of candidate_version on accepted requests, with no more than 8 internal states.
design_brief.md must describe the module's intended behavior (monotonic anti-rollback versioning) in purely functional terms without disclosing any anomaly.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing a list of candidate anomalies, per-candidate confidence scores, and rationale referencing specific signals/states in version_ctrl.v

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json MUST be valid JSON with top-level fields: 'candidates' (array), 'summary' (string), and 'tool_version' (string).
Each element of 'candidates' MUST include the fields: 'id' (string), 'description' (string), 'confidence' (number in [0,1]), 'trigger_condition' (string), and 'payload_effect' (string).

At least one candidate entry MUST reference the specific register(s)/state variable(s) in version_ctrl.v responsible for tracking the sequence of accepted requests (i.e., name the internal signal(s) used, not just 'some internal logic').

The report MUST state, for the highest-confidence candidate, the exact update expression asserted in the terminal/triggering condition (e.g., what value version_q is assigned to instead of the expected max(version_q, candidate_version)).

public_spec.interface: Module under analysis: version_ctrl, defined in inputs/version_ctrl.v. Ports: input wire clk (system clock, rising-edge sequential), input wire rst_n (active-low asynchronous reset), input wire req_valid (asserted for one cycle to present a candidate update request), input wire [7:0] candidate_version (public candidate firmware version presented with req_valid), input wire req_accept (external signal indicating the request passed signature/authenticity checks; only accepted requests may affect state), output reg [7:0] version_q (the current, publicly-observable committed firmware version register), output wire update_ack (asserted for one cycle the cycle after an accepted request is processed, Mealy-style relative to req_valid/req_accept AND one-cycle delayed registered output). All ports are public (no secret-bearing signals). The participant does NOT modify version_ctrl.v. The participant's deliverable is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json conforming to the schema given in response_format. evaluate.py reads inputs/version_ctrl.v for reference (and may optionally simulate it with iverilog/vvp or analyze it with yosys) and grades the content of submission/trojan_report.json against hidden ground truth.
public_spec.objective: A firmware update controller module manages an 8-bit monotonic firmware version register used to prevent installation of older, vulnerable firmware images. Analyze the provided RTL implementation of this version-control module and produce an analysis report describing its update logic, including any conditions under which the version register could be set to a value other than the maximum of the current and candidate version (as required for correct anti-rollback behavior). Identify any suspicious internal state tracking, undocumented signal dependencies, or conditions that cause non-monotonic or unexpected updates to the version register, and report them as candidate anomalies with supporting rationale.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
